title: Runtime: add apply/rollback lease locking + propagation status reporting (Optimize config)
author: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Context: as part of Safe apply + rollback for Optimize config changes, we need runtime-side protection against concurrent applies/rollbacks and a reliable way to surface propagation progress/failures back to the control plane/Console. Previously, the control plane attempted to serialize requests, but we still saw overlapping apply attempts in practice (retries + partial propagation + operator double-clicks) and we had no structured status beyond a single “apply succeeded/failed” response from the first hop.

This PR adds: (1) a distributed lease/lock that is acquired by each runtime cluster before mutating optimization config, (2) an apply operation state machine with periodic status heartbeats back to the control plane, and (3) baseline metrics for apply/rollback latency and failure modes.

Locking/lease design: each apply/rollback is scoped to (cluster_id, optimize_scope_key) where optimize_scope_key is the resolved scope we apply to at runtime (route+model+tenant+region resolved into a single canonical key). Before applying, runtime attempts to acquire a lease via the internal LockService (backed by Redis, TTL-based). Leases are renewed while an operation is in-flight; if renewal fails, the operation is aborted before the “commit” step (see below). A lease is required for: config apply, rollback apply, and cache invalidation steps that materially affect request execution. We explicitly do not require a lease for “read-only” config fetches.

Operation semantics: runtime now treats apply/rollback as an operation with phases: RECEIVED -> FETCHED_CONFIG -> VALIDATED -> QUIESCED (stop accepting new work for the scope / drain batching queues) -> INVALIDATED_CACHES (KV/prefix caches as applicable) -> APPLIED (swap config atomically) -> WARMED (optional: minimal warmup pass for quantization profile swaps / scheduler knobs) -> COMPLETED. On failure we emit FAILED with a categorized reason (LOCK_ACQUIRE_FAILED, LEASE_LOST, VALIDATION_FAILED, APPLY_COMMIT_FAILED, CACHE_INVALIDATION_FAILED, WARMUP_TIMEOUT).

Status reporting: runtime emits status events to the control plane endpoint /internal/optimize/config/operations/{op_id}/status. Events include: op_id, scope_key, cluster_id, target_version_id, phase, timestamps, and optional error details (sanitized). This is intentionally append-only from runtime’s perspective; the control plane is responsible for de-duping by (op_id, phase) and projecting the latest state for Console.

Atomicity notes: the actual “commit” step is a single atomic pointer swap inside runtime’s config registry (ConfigRegistry::set_active(scope_key, new_version)). All other steps are pre-commit and can be retried safely as long as the lease is held. If we lose the lease after commit, we still complete the operation but emit a warning event (LEASE_LOST_POST_COMMIT) so SRE can correlate to potential overlap risk. Follow-up work will tighten this by making renewal required until COMPLETED, but this is sufficient for preventing the known double-apply failure mode we saw last month.

Metrics/observability: adds optimize_config_apply_inflight{cluster_id}, optimize_config_operation_duration_seconds{phase, outcome}, optimize_config_lease_acquire_duration_seconds{outcome}, optimize_config_lease_renew_failures_total, and optimize_config_status_post_failures_total. Also emits structured logs with correlation_id/op_id for incident-bot linking.

Testing: adds unit tests for lease acquisition/renewal and the operation phase transitions; adds an integration test that simulates a competing apply (second requester gets 409 Conflict with current_op_id); and a failure-mode test that forces lease renewal failure mid-operation and asserts we never reach APPLIED.

Rollout/compatibility: guarded behind runtime feature flag optimize.runtime_apply_lease_v1 (default off). Control plane can send status events even if it doesn’t yet render them; events are tolerated. This PR is designed to be deployed before Console wiring so we can validate behavior in internal clusters.

Risk: cache invalidation behavior is sensitive; we only invalidate KV/prefix caches when config changes touch batching/cache knobs or quantization profile id. For unrelated config fields, we skip invalidation to avoid unnecessary latency impact.

Refs: ENG-4827; pairs with PRs adding the control plane store/API and validator. Notes from the incident thread (latency spike after optimization tweak) are captured in ENG-4827 acceptance criteria.

review_conversation: Mateo Alvarez: Can we confirm the lock scope matches exactly what runtime applies (post-resolution)? We had issues where control plane keys != runtime keys.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Yep — added OptimizeScopeKey::fromResolved() and we only lock on the canonical resolved key. Also included key in every status event for correlation.
Sofia Ivanova: Concern: QUIESCED step could stall if batching queues never drain under load. Do we have a timeout + fallback?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added a bounded drain timeout (default 10s) with explicit FAILED(WARMUP_TIMEOUT) vs FAILED(QUIESCE_TIMEOUT). For now we fail rather than force-apply; SRE can retry or rollback. We can discuss a force option later.
Neha Kapoor: What happens if lease renew fails after commit? That’s the scary case for split brain.

Omar El-Sayed (author): We don’t revert automatically in this PR. We emit LEASE_LOST_POST_COMMIT and continue posting status so control plane can block new operations until things converge. Follow-up proposal: treat renew failure as fatal pre-commit only; post-commit renew failure will trigger an immediate “lockdown” mode for that scope.
Allison Grant: Please add labels to the new metrics and make sure cardinality is safe. cluster_id is okay; do not include tenant id.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Done — no tenant labels; scope_key is only in logs/status payload, not Prometheus labels.
Chloe Martin: Status endpoint path: can we align to control-plane naming in ENG-4822/4823? Right now this uses /internal/optimize/config/operations/…

Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated to match the control-plane stub used in the API scaffold (kept internal prefix). Also added a compatibility shim to tolerate 404 during rollout and degrade to logs-only.
Mateo Alvarez: Approved after the quiesce timeout change + metric label cleanup.
Neha Kapoor: Approved; please file follow-up for post-commit lease loss handling + runbook notes.
follow_ups: ENG-4896: handle LEASE_LOST_POST_COMMIT by blocking subsequent operations until reconciliation

release_notes: Internal-only: runtime now serializes Optimize config apply/rollback per scope using a lease and reports per-phase propagation status to the control plane. Guarded by optimize.runtime_apply_lease_v1.
